Reproducing Bouchard et al. (2013) from dandiset 000019¶

Paper. Bouchard KE, Mesgarani N, Johnson K, Chang EF (2013). Functional organization of human sensorimotor cortex for speech articulation. Nature 495, 327-332. doi:10.1038/nature11911. The claims file (claims/000019/10.1038-nature11911.yaml) was written from the NIH author manuscript in PubMed Central (PMC3606666) with its supplement, and checked by a second reader.

Dandiset. DANDI:000019, "Human ECoG speaking consonant-vowel syllables", version 0.220126.2148. The paper cites no version of the dandiset (it predates it). This is the only published version; the draft has the same 31 assets and the same size, so the published version is pinned.

What the dandiset holds. Raw ECoG (256 channels, 3051.76 Hz) of 31 recording blocks from four subjects (EC2, EC9, GP31, GP33), with a trial table per block (syllable, start, C-V transition and stop times), a bad flag and an anatomical label per electrode, 3-D electrode coordinates for two subjects, and a rest period per block. The microphone signal was removed (dandiset description), and no high gamma is stored, so high gamma is computed here from the raw voltage. The paper's subjects are EC2, EC33 and EC31; EC2, GP33 and GP31 are taken to be them (see the data check). EC9 is not in the paper and is not analysed.

Readings. Where the claims file leaves a method detail open it names readings, and every reading is run; a claim's outcome is the one all its method readings give, and it is blocked as methods_underspecified when they differ. The first run of this attempt asked five questions (questions/000019.yaml), answered by a reader on 2026-10-22, and the claims file now names these readings, all run here:

  • the baseline of the z-scores: (a) pre, -1000 to -500 ms before each C-V transition; (b) whole, the whole block; (c) rest, the rest period the dataset marks as baseline (a reading since the answer; the first run showed it as a variant only);
  • the CVs averaged: (a) every CV the dataset holds (all); (b) only CVs with 15 or more renditions (15+); the paper does not say which;
  • the z-scoring before the PCA: row, each electrode's whole concatenated (CV x time) series; time, each electrode across CVs at each time; the paper does not say which;
  • the input projected onto the PCs to give the states: (i) the z-scored matrix given to the PCA; (ii) the baseline z-scored high gamma, as Methods Eq. 5 writes it (added with the answer);
  • the acoustic onset of fig3d: the dandiset has no audio, and the hand-marked syllable start may stand in for it as a deviation, with the result against t = 0 shown beside it (the answer).

The fifth answer says the paper gives no way to derive the distances from the central sulcus and Sylvian fissure from grid geometry or unlabelled coordinates, so the spatial claims stay blocked.

import itertools
import time
import warnings

import h5py
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import remfile
from scipy import stats
from scipy.cluster.hierarchy import fcluster, linkage
from scipy.spatial.distance import pdist, squareform
from sklearn.metrics import silhouette_score

import bouchard as B

# Metadata of every file (EC9 included), and a fingerprint of its first samples, read by streaming.
ASSETS = B.assets()
meta_rows = []
for a in ASSETS:
    with h5py.File(remfile.File(a["url"]), "r") as h5:
        m = B.read_metadata(h5)
        m["fingerprint"] = h5["acquisition/ElectricalSeries/data"][:2000, :4].copy()
    m["path"], m["size"] = a["path"], a["size"]
    meta_rows.append(m)
print(f"read metadata of {len(meta_rows)} files of dandiset {B.DANDISET_ID} version {B.DANDISET_VERSION} "
      f"in {time.time() - started:.0f} s")

# High gamma of the three subjects of the paper: every block is streamed into memory and processed.
blocks = {}
for s in B.SUBJECTS:
    blocks[s] = B.process_blocks([a for a in ASSETS if a["path"].startswith(f"sub-{s}/")],
                                 log=lambda msg: None)
S = {s: B.load_subject(blocks[s]) for s in B.SUBJECTS}
# What each file holds besides the tables: from the processed files in memory, and for EC9 (not
# analysed) from its first file, streamed.
CONTENTS = {a["path"]: b["contents"] for s in B.SUBJECTS for a, b in zip([a for a in ASSETS if a["path"].startswith(f"sub-{s}/")], blocks[s])}
ec9 = next(a for a in ASSETS if a["path"].startswith("sub-EC9/"))
with h5py.File(remfile.File(ec9["url"]), "r") as h5:
    CONTENTS[ec9["path"]] = B.describe_file(h5)
print(f"processed {sum(len(v) for v in blocks.values())} blocks in {time.time() - started:.0f} s")
streamed = sum(a["size"] for a in ASSETS if a["path"].split("/")[0][4:] in B.SUBJECTS)
print(f"streamed {streamed / 1e9:.1f} GB of raw ECoG")

# Duplicates: blocks with the same length, the same trial table, or the same first samples.
pairs = []
for i, j in itertools.combinations(range(len(meta_rows)), 2):
    a, b = meta_rows[i], meta_rows[j]
    same_n = a["n_samples"] == b["n_samples"]
    same_trials = len(a["cv"]) == len(b["cv"]) and np.allclose(a["cv"], b["cv"])
    same_data = np.array_equal(a["fingerprint"], b["fingerprint"])
    if same_n or same_trials or same_data:
        pairs.append((a["path"], b["path"], same_n, same_trials, same_data))
print("Pairs sharing sample count, trial times or first 2000 samples of 4 channels:")
for p in pairs:
    print("  ", p)

# Syllables per subject, from the trial labels.
label_rows = []
for m in meta_rows:
    for c in m["condition"]:
        label_rows.append({"subject": m["subject"], "label": c, "cv": B.parse_label(c)})
labels = pd.DataFrame(label_rows)
for s, g in labels.groupby("subject"):
    unparsed = g[g.cv.isna()].label.value_counts().to_dict()
    cv = g.dropna().cv
    cons = sorted({c for c, v in cv}, key=B.CONSONANTS.index)
    counts = cv.value_counts()
    print(f"{s}: {len(g)} trials, {counts.size} distinct CVs, {len(cons)} consonants; renditions per CV "
          f"{counts.min()} to {counts.max()}; labels that are not CVs of the task: {unparsed}")
    missing = [c + v for c in B.CONSONANTS for v in "aiu" if (c, v) not in set(cv)]
    print(f"    CVs missing: {missing}; CVs with fewer than 15 renditions: "
          f"{ {''.join(k): int(n) for k, n in counts.items() if n < 15} }; more than 100: "
          f"{ {''.join(k): int(n) for k, n in counts.items() if n > 100} }")
print("Labels merged as misspellings:", labels[labels.label.isin(list(B.SPELLING))].groupby(["subject", "label"]).size().to_dict())
print("Spellings merged: 'she' -> 'shee', 'ha' -> 'haa'. Paper: 19, 19 and 18 consonants, 168 CVs (57 + 57 + 54), 15 to 100 renditions each.")

The archive's summary counts four subjects. EC2 matches the paper's EC2 by name. GP31 and GP33 are not names the paper uses; the paper's other two subjects are EC31 (left hemisphere) and EC33 (right). No field in the files links them: the subject fields hold only the species and the subject id, and the session descriptions name only the block (printed above). In EC2 and GP31 the electrode group is named L256Grid electrodes, and every electrode has a negative x; both fit a left hemisphere if the L and the x mean what they usually do. GP33's group is auto_group, with location location, and GP33 has no coordinates, so its hemisphere cannot be checked. GP31 is the subject with 18 consonants that have all three vowels (/tha/ and /thu/ are missing, table of data-composition), which fits the paper's subject with 18 consonants and 54 CVs. That GP31 is EC31 and GP33 is EC33 is an assumption the data are consistent with, not shown by them. EC9 has 23 consonant labels (including /ch/, /dh/, /j/, /sk/), labels on only 79 of 256 electrodes and no coordinates; it is not one of the paper's subjects and is left out.

Besides the raw series, one file (EC2 block 1) has a processing module holding a power spectrum of the 256 channels (frequency by channel, no time axis); no file holds audio or a microphone series. The kept trials whose epoch overlaps an interval marked as an ECoG artifact are counted once per trial (162); counted once per trial and interval, as in the first version of this check, they are 177.

Units: the raw series says volts with a conversion factor of 0.001, so by NWB the stored values times 0.001 are volts. The stored values have an SD of a few 1e-5 (printed above): read as volts this is tens of microvolts, a usual ECoG amplitude, while with the factor it would be tens of nanovolts. The data are consistent with values already in volts and a wrong conversion factor; this does not affect the analysis, which uses z-scores only. Sampling rate 3051.7578 Hz in all files, the TDT rate the Methods round to 3052 Hz. The pre baseline (-1000 to -500 ms before each C-V transition) has a median mean within a few percent of the whole block's. The rest periods are short (3.3 to 78 s per block) and their statistics differ from the whole block's in both directions by block (median ratios above); z-scores against them reach higher maxima (ranges above). The rest period is baseline reading (c) of the claims file.

# Clock check: the trial times and the ECoG share a clock if the high gamma tells syllables apart
# at the times the paper says, and not before speech. Leave-one-out nearest-centroid classification
# of the vowel (/a/, /i/, /u/) and of the major oral articulator of the consonant (labial, coronal,
# dorsal; reading (a) of the labels) from the vSMC high-gamma pattern of each CV, at each time.
def loo_accuracy(X, y):
    ok = 0
    for i in range(len(y)):
        mask = np.arange(len(y)) != i
        cents = {c: X[mask & (y == c)].mean(0) for c in np.unique(y[mask])}
        pred = min(cents, key=lambda c: np.linalg.norm(X[i] - cents[c]))
        ok += pred == y[i]
    return ok / len(y)

clock = []
for s in B.SUBJECTS:
    H = S[s]["H"]["pre"][:, S[s]["vsmc"]]
    vow = np.array([v for c, v in S[s]["cvs"]])
    maj = np.array([B.MAJOR["a"].get(c, "") for c, v in S[s]["cvs"]])
    lab = maj != ""
    for t in range(0, len(B.EPOCH_MS), 5):
        clock.append({"subject": s, "t_ms": B.EPOCH_MS[t], "vowel": loo_accuracy(H[:, :, t], vow),
                      "consonant": loo_accuracy(H[lab][:, :, t], maj[lab])})
clock = pd.DataFrame(clock)
summary = clock.groupby("t_ms")[["vowel", "consonant"]].mean()
print("Mean accuracy over subjects (chance 1/3 for vowels; 0.5 to 0.53 for consonants, the largest class share):")
print(summary.iloc[::4].round(2).T.to_string())
for col in ["vowel", "consonant"]:
    print(f"{col}: peak {summary[col].max():.2f} at {summary[col].idxmax()} ms; mean before -400 ms {summary[col][summary.index < -400].mean():.2f}")
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(6, 3))
summary.plot(ax=ax)
ax.axvline(0, color="k", lw=0.5)
ax.set_xlabel("time from C-V transition (ms)"); ax.set_ylabel("LOO accuracy")
plt.show()

The consonant's articulator is decoded best before the C-V transition (0.89 at -75 ms) and the vowel after it (0.83 at 250 ms), and both are near chance at the start of the epoch (vowel 0.39 against 1/3; consonant 0.59 against a largest-class share of about 0.5). This is consistent with the trial times and the ECoG sharing a clock in every subject, with the annotations marking the C-V transition; it does not show the alignment to the millisecond.

Shared computations¶

The partial correlations and the GLM (Methods Eqs. 2 to 4) are computed once per baseline and CV set, and the state space (Methods Eq. 5) once per baseline, CV set and z-scoring reading; the states K of each CV are then projected from the PCA input (reading i) or from the baseline z-scored high gamma (reading ii). The articulator windows T_A come from the timing analysis under each of its eight readings (claim fig3d-timing-sequence: threshold set per subject or pooled, over all six articulators or per articulator, and onset at the threshold or at half the peak).

In [11]:
BASES = B.BASELINES      # baseline readings (a) pre, (b) whole, (c) rest (claims header)
ZMODES = ("row", "time")  # z-scoring before the PCA (claims header)
PROJ = ("i", "ii")        # input projected: (i) the PCA input, (ii) Hg as Eq. 5 writes it
ART6 = B.ARTICULATORS + B.VOWEL_ARTICULATORS
TIMING_READINGS = list(itertools.product(("per subject", "pooled"), ("all six", "per articulator"), ("threshold", "half peak")))
CVSETS = ("all", "15+")    # (a) every CV, (b) only CVs with at least 15 renditions (claims header)
CVIDX = {(s, cs): np.where(S[s]["counts"] >= (15 if cs == "15+" else 0))[0] for s in B.SUBJECTS for cs in CVSETS}
CVS = {k: [S[k[0]]["cvs"][i] for i in v] for k, v in CVIDX.items()}
AM = {k: B.articulator_matrix(v) for k, v in CVS.items()}
HV = {(s, base, cs): S[s]["H"][base][CVIDX[s, cs]][:, S[s]["vsmc"]]
      for s in B.SUBJECTS for base in B.BASELINES for cs in CVSETS}
RHO = {(s, base, cs): B.partial_correlation(HV[s, base, cs], AM[s, cs]) for s in B.SUBJECTS for base in BASES for cs in CVSETS}
GLM = {(s, base, cs): B.glm(HV[s, base, cs], AM[s, cs][:, :4]) for s in B.SUBJECTS for base in BASES for cs in CVSETS}


def timing_rows(base, cs, reading, rho=None):
    rho = RHO if rho is None else rho
    subj_mode, art_mode, onset_mode = reading
    rows = []
    for s in B.SUBJECTS:
        pool = np.concatenate([rho[x, base, cs] for x in B.SUBJECTS]) if subj_mode == "pooled" else rho[s, base, cs]
        for a in range(6):
            vals = pool if art_mode == "all six" else pool[:, a]
            thr = vals.mean() + 2.5 * vals.std()
            for e in range(rho[s, base, cs].shape[0]):
                r = rho[s, base, cs][e, a]
                if r.max() > thr:
                    on, pk, off = B.timing(r, thr if onset_mode == "threshold" else r.max() / 2)
                    rows.append({"subject": s, "articulator": ART6[a], "electrode": e, "onset": on,
                                 "peak": pk, "offset": off, "threshold": thr})
    return pd.DataFrame(rows)


TIMING = {(base, cs, r): timing_rows(base, cs, r) for base in BASES for cs in CVSETS for r in TIMING_READINGS}


def articulator_windows(base, cs, reading):
    """T_A per subject: mean onset to mean offset of the subject's electrodes for A (None if none)."""
    t = TIMING[base, cs, reading]
    out = {}
    for s in B.SUBJECTS:
        for a in B.ARTICULATORS:
            g = t[(t.subject == s) & (t.articulator == a)]
            out[s, a] = (g.onset.mean(), g.offset.mean()) if len(g) else None
    return out


def weights(base, cs, reading, pmode):
    """Per subject: W (vSMC electrode, 4), NaN for an articulator without a window, and the
    electrodes kept by the GLM rule (mean p over T_A below 0.05 for any articulator)."""
    T = articulator_windows(base, cs, reading)
    out = {}
    for s in B.SUBJECTS:
        beta, pF, pt, r2 = GLM[s, base, cs]
        keep = np.zeros(beta.shape[0], bool)
        W = np.full((beta.shape[0], 4), np.nan)
        for a, name in enumerate(B.ARTICULATORS):
            if T[s, name] is None:
                continue
            idx = (B.EPOCH_MS >= T[s, name][0]) & (B.EPOCH_MS <= T[s, name][1])
            p = (pF[:, idx] if pmode == "F-test" else pt[:, a, idx]).mean(1)
            keep |= p < 0.05
            W[:, a] = beta[:, a, idx].mean(1)
        out[s] = {"W": W, "keep": keep, "windows": {a: T[s, a] for a in B.ARTICULATORS}}
    return out


W_READINGS = [(base, cs, r, p) for base in BASES for cs in CVSETS for r in TIMING_READINGS for p in ("F-test", "t-test")]
WEIGHTS = {k: weights(*k) for k in W_READINGS}
STATE = {(s, base, z, cs, w): B.state_space(HV[s, base, cs], z, w)
         for s in B.SUBJECTS for base in BASES for z in ZMODES for cs in CVSETS
         for w in [(-500, 750), (-375, 620)]}
EP = (-500, 750)
SS_READINGS = list(itertools.product(BASES, ZMODES, PROJ, CVSETS))
KS = {(s, base, z, pj, cs): STATE[s, base, z, cs, EP][2] if pj == "i" else B.project(STATE[s, base, z, cs, EP][0], HV[s, base, cs])
      for s in B.SUBJECTS for base, z, pj, cs in SS_READINGS}

# Variant (not a reading of the claims file): the trials whose epoch overlaps an interval the files
# mark as an ECoG artifact are left out of the CV means; the CVs and electrodes are the same.
S_CLEAN = {s: B.load_subject(blocks[s], exclude_invalid=True) for s in B.SUBJECTS}
assert all(S_CLEAN[s]["cvs"] == S[s]["cvs"] and S_CLEAN[s]["counts"].min() > 0 for s in B.SUBJECTS)
HV_CLEAN = {(s, base, cs): S_CLEAN[s]["H"][base][CVIDX[s, cs]][:, S[s]["vsmc"]]
            for s in B.SUBJECTS for base in B.BASELINES for cs in CVSETS}
print("Renditions left out by the artifact variant, per subject:", {s: int((S[s]["counts"] - S_CLEAN[s]["counts"]).sum()) for s in B.SUBJECTS},
      "| largest share of one CV's renditions:", {s: round(float(((S[s]["counts"] - S_CLEAN[s]["counts"]) / S[s]["counts"]).max()), 2) for s in B.SUBJECTS})
print(f"shared computations done at {time.time() - started:.0f} s")

data-composition¶

Three subjects with high-density ECoG (two left, one right hemisphere) read aloud CV syllables made of 18 or 19 consonants followed by /a/, /i/ or /u/, each CV produced 15 to 100 times, with the microphone recorded with the ECoG at 3052 Hz.

Result: partially reproduced. The dandiset holds the three subjects (taking GP31 and GP33 to be EC31 and EC33) and a fourth one, EC9, that is not in the paper. The ECoG rate is 3051.76 Hz. The counts differ from the paper's: 57, 55 and 57 CVs (169 in all, against 168), each subject with 19 consonants, and renditions of 2 to 107 per CV (EC2's /thi/ 10, GP31's /thi/ 2, GP31 up to 107). Leaving out CVs with fewer than 15 renditions gives 56 + 54 + 57 = 167, still not the paper's split. The audio is not in the dandiset, and GP33's hemisphere cannot be checked. In EC2 and GP31, 18 consonants have all three vowels with 15 or more renditions each, and in GP33 19; the paper's split is 19, 19 and 18 consonants.

active-electrodes¶

About 30 active vSMC electrodes were found per subject during syllable articulation, an electrode being active when its high-gamma z-score changed by more than 2 for any syllable.

In [13]:
def overall(outcomes):
    """The outcome all method readings give, or methods_underspecified when they differ."""
    u = sorted(set(outcomes))
    return u[0] if len(u) == 1 else "differ by reading: " + ", ".join(f"{o} {list(outcomes).count(o)}" for o in u)


def by_factor(df, factors, col="outcome"):
    """Outcome counts for each level of each reading factor, the other factors pooled."""
    print(f"Outcome counts by reading factor ({len(df)} readings):")
    for f in factors:
        print(f"  {f}:", {lvl: g[col].value_counts().to_dict() for lvl, g in df.groupby(f, sort=False)})

Result: blocked (methods_underspecified). The two readings of the CV set give different outcomes. With every CV, no baseline gives a mean within 27 to 33: 24.3 per subject with pre (EC2 15, GP31 49, GP33 9), 21.3 with whole and 34.0 with rest (not reproduced). With only the CVs of 15 or more renditions, rest gives 27.0 (EC2 29, GP31 31, GP33 21), at the lower edge of the tolerance, while pre gives 10.7 and whole 7.0 (partially reproduced). Both readings of the change give the same counts, as no electrode passes on a decrease alone. The count moves strongly with the threshold (with every CV, 41.7 to 5.3 per subject over thresholds 1.5 to 3 with pre).

The split between the CV readings comes from one syllable. Every GP31 electrode that is active with every CV but not with the 15+ CVs is above 2 for /thi/, which GP31 has 2 renditions of (40 electrodes under pre, 43 under whole, 20 under rest); in EC2 one electrode is active through /thi/ (10 renditions) under pre and rest, and in GP33 none. Leaving out the trials that overlap intervals marked as ECoG artifacts (a variant, not a reading of the claims file) gives means of 22.7, 21.0 and 26.0 with every CV and 8.0, 6.7 and 15.0 with the 15+ CVs, none within 27 to 33. GP31's count under rest with the 15+ CVs falls from 31 to 2 in this variant, so the one reading within tolerance rests on trials the files mark as artifacts.

fig1c-e-articulator-electrodes¶

In one subject, dorsal electrodes (e124, e108) were active for /b/ (lips), mid vSMC electrodes (e129, e133, e105) for /d/ (front tongue), and a more ventral electrode (e104) was most active for /g/ (back tongue).

Subject and numbering pairs that put all six named electrodes on vSMC: []

Result: blocked (metadata_insufficient). No subject, counted from 1 or from 0, has all six named electrodes on vSMC. The most is 5 of 6, in EC2 counted from 0, where e129 is labelled middle temporal; GP31 has at most 4 and GP33 at most 3. The criterion blocks the claim in that case: the dataset does not say which subject Fig. 1 shows or how the paper numbered electrodes. For information, in EC2 counted from 1 (3 of 6 on vSMC, e124 flagged bad in some block), five of the six named electrodes prefer their syllable under both measures and all three baselines; counted from 0, two or three of six do.

fig1f-h-phonetic-contrasts¶

Fricatives with different tongue-tip constriction locations engaged different electrodes; front-tongue consonants of different manner engaged overlapping electrodes with different magnitudes; for /ja/, /ji/, /ju/ the activity was similar before the C-V transition, while a dorsal electrode was active during /u/ only.

The judged part: in at least one subject, a vSMC electrode with a positive lips weight (from the GLM electrodes of claim fig2a-lips-dorsal) has mean high gamma above 2 at +250 ms for /ju/ and below 2 for /ja/ and /ji/. The lips weights and the GLM electrodes are computed without electrode positions, which are only needed for fig2a's spatial judgement (see the summary).

t250 = B.ms_index(250)
fh = []
for key in W_READINGS:
    base, cs = key[0], key[1]
    hits = {}
    for s in B.SUBJECTS:
        cvs = CVS[s, cs]
        Hj = {v: HV[s, base, cs][cvs.index(("y", v)), :, t250] for v in "aiu"}
        w = WEIGHTS[key][s]
        cand = w["keep"] & (w["W"][:, 0] > 0)
        hit = cand & (Hj["u"] > 2) & (Hj["a"] < 2) & (Hj["i"] < 2)
        hits[s] = (int(cand.sum()), int((cand & (Hj["u"] > 2)).sum()), int(hit.sum()),
                   float(Hj["u"][cand].max()) if cand.any() else np.nan)
    fh.append({"baseline": base, "CVs": cs, "timing reading": " / ".join(key[2]), "p-value": key[3],
               **{f"{s} lips+ / ju>2 / hits / max /ju/": f"{hits[s][0]} / {hits[s][1]} / {hits[s][2]} / {hits[s][3]:.2f}" for s in B.SUBJECTS},
               "ju>2": sum(h[1] for h in hits.values()), "holds": any(h[2] > 0 for h in hits.values())})
fh = pd.DataFrame(fh)
print(fh.to_string(index=False))
print("\nReadings where it holds:", int(fh.holds.sum()), "of", len(fh))
print("Largest /ju/ z at +250 ms among lips-positive GLM electrodes, over all readings and subjects:",
      max(float(v.split(" / ")[3]) for c in fh.columns if "max /ju/" in c for v in fh[c]))
print("Readings with a lips-positive GLM electrode above 2 for /ju/:", int((fh["ju>2"] > 0).sum()), "of", len(fh),
      "(baselines:", fh[fh["ju>2"] > 0].baseline.value_counts().to_dict(), "); in all of them /ja/ or /ji/ is also above 2 there" if not fh.holds.any() else "")
print("Outcome over readings:", overall(["reproduced" if h else "not reproduced" for h in fh.holds]))

                         "/ju/ > 2, /ja/ and /ji/ < 2": int(((Hj["u"] > 2) & (Hj["a"] < 2) & (Hj["i"] < 2)).sum()),

for ax, s in zip(axes, B.SUBJECTS):
    cvs = CVS[s, "all"]
    H = HV[s, "pre", "all"]
    w = WEIGHTS[key0][s]
    cand = np.where(w["keep"] & (w["W"][:, 0] > 0))[0]
    d = H[cvs.index(("y", "u")), cand, t250] - np.maximum(H[cvs.index(("y", "a")), cand, t250], H[cvs.index(("y", "i")), cand, t250])
    e = cand[np.argmax(d)]
    tr = H[[cvs.index(("y", v)) for v in "aiu"], e]
    for v, row in zip("aiu", tr):
        ax.plot(B.EPOCH_MS, row, label=f"/j{v}/")
    ax.set_title(f"{s} electrode {S[s]['vsmc'][e]}")
    print(f"{s}: plotted electrode {S[s]['vsmc'][e]} (largest /ju/ minus /ja/,/ji/ at +250 ms among lips+ GLM electrodes), z at +250 ms: "

          f"mean |difference| between the three before 0 ms {np.abs(tr[:, B.EPOCH_MS < 0] - tr[:, B.EPOCH_MS < 0].mean(0)).mean():.2f}")
    ax.axvline(0, color="k", lw=0.5); ax.axhline(2, color="grey", lw=0.5, ls="--")

Result: not reproduced. Under all 96 readings (three baselines, two CV sets, eight timing readings for T_A, two p-value readings) no GLM electrode with a positive lips weight has z above 2 for /ju/ at +250 ms and below 2 for /ja/ and /ji/. With the rest baseline some do exceed 2 for /ju/ (13 of 96 readings, largest 3.54), but at each of them /ja/ or /ji/ is above 2 as well; under pre and whole none reaches 2. The /ju/ responses of the plotted electrodes are larger than /ja/ and /ji/ at +250 ms, but under the threshold. Without the GLM selection, among all vSMC electrodes, one EC2 electrode under rest (both CV sets) has /ju/ above 2 and /ja/ and /ji/ below 2; under pre and whole no vSMC electrode in any subject reaches 2 for /ju/ (largest 1.19), so there the result does not come from the selection. The other parts of the claim are not judged (no measure in the paper).

Spatial claims (blocked)¶

fig2a-lips-dorsal, fig2b-somatotopic-sequence, suppfig3b-spatial-clustering, suppfig3d-cross-subject, suppfig3f-dv-sequence, suppfig5-intermediate-organization and suppfig7-no-latency-difference all need each electrode's anterior-posterior distance from the central sulcus and dorsal-ventral distance from the Sylvian fissure (Methods). The dandiset gives neither. EC2 and GP31 have x, y, z coordinates with no unit, frame or description; GP33, one of the three subjects, has none. The labels say precentral or postcentral, not how far from either sulcus, and no electrode is labelled as on the guenon. Asked whether the paper gives a way to obtain these distances from the grid geometry, the reader answered that it does not: the paper measures them on each subject's MRI reconstruction. These claims stay blocked as metadata_insufficient.

The GLM electrode selection and weights of fig2a-lips-dorsal do not need positions and are computed above. For information only (not an outcome, and not a reading of the claim), the median z coordinate of the top 10% of each articulator's weights in the two subjects that have coordinates, under the first reading:

    w = WEIGHTS[key0][s]
    z = S[s]["z"][S[s]["vsmc"]]
    kept = np.where(w["keep"])[0]
    out = []
    for a, name in enumerate(B.ARTICULATORS):
        if np.isnan(w["W"][kept, a]).all():
            out.append(f"{name} no window"); continue
        top = kept[np.argsort(-w["W"][kept, a])[:max(1, len(kept) // 10)]]
        out.append(f"{name} {np.median(z[top]):.1f}")
    print(f"{s}: {len(kept)} GLM electrodes; median z of top 10% weights: " + ", ".join(out))

suppfig6-mixed-tuning¶

Single electrodes show a clear preferred articulator and also carry weights for other articulators.

In [17]:
def mixed_tuning(Wk):
    """The criterion on weights Wk (electrode, 4): holds, group means, electrodes without a positive weight."""
    Wk = np.nan_to_num(Wk, nan=-np.inf)
    pos = np.where(Wk > 0, Wk, 0)
    has = pos.sum(1) > 0
    pct = 100 * pos[has] / pos[has].sum(1, keepdims=True)
    pref = np.argmax(Wk[has], axis=1)
    groups, ok = {}, True
    for a in range(4):
        g = pct[pref == a]
        if len(g) == 0:
            groups[B.ARTICULATORS[a]] = "none"
            continue
        m = g.mean(0)
        ok &= bool(np.argmax(m) == a and (np.delete(m, a) > 0).any())
        groups[B.ARTICULATORS[a]] = f"n={len(g)} " + "/".join(f"{x:.0f}" for x in m)
    return ok, groups, int((~has).sum())


rng6 = np.random.default_rng(6)
s6 = []
for key in W_READINGS:
    Wk = np.concatenate([WEIGHTS[key][s]["W"][WEIGHTS[key][s]["keep"]] for s in B.SUBJECTS])
    no_window = int(np.isnan(Wk).any(1).sum())
    # Null: each articulator's weights permuted across the subject's GLM electrodes, which breaks any
    # tuning of single electrodes while keeping each articulator's distribution of weights.
    Wnull = np.concatenate([np.column_stack([rng6.permutation(col) for col in WEIGHTS[key][s]["W"][WEIGHTS[key][s]["keep"]].T])
                            for s in B.SUBJECTS])
    null_ok = mixed_tuning(Wnull)[0]
    ok, groups, no_pos = mixed_tuning(Wk)
    s6.append({"baseline": key[0], "CVs": key[1], "timing reading": " / ".join(key[2]), "p-value": key[3],
               "electrodes": int(len(Wk)), "with an articulator lacking T_A": no_window,
               "no positive weight": no_pos, **groups, "holds": ok, "holds on permuted weights": null_ok})
s6 = pd.DataFrame(s6)
print("Group means of positive weights as % (Lips/Tongue/Larynx/Jaw), electrodes grouped by largest W:")

Readings where it holds: 96 of 96
Lips group: preferred share 63 to 79% over the 96 readings with such electrodes
Tongue group: preferred share 48 to 96% over the 95 readings with such electrodes
Larynx group: preferred share 49 to 84% over the 96 readings with such electrodes
Jaw group: preferred share 69 to 84% over the 96 readings with such electrodes
GLM electrodes over the three subjects: 49 to 117
Outcome over readings: reproduced
Null, the same test on weights permuted across electrodes (one permutation per reading): holds in 94 of 96

Result: reproduced. Under all 96 readings each group's preferred articulator has the largest mean share of positive weight (Lips 63 to 79%, Tongue 48 to 96%, Larynx 49 to 84%, Jaw 69 to 84%), and the other articulators keep a non-zero share (table). In one reading no electrode prefers the tongue, so that group is absent there. The GLM electrodes number 49 to 117 over the three subjects. In readings where an articulator has no window T_A in a subject, its weights there are missing and those electrodes are grouped on the other articulators. The test barely discriminates: on weights permuted across each subject's electrodes, which removes any tuning of single electrodes, it holds in 94 of 96 readings, because grouping electrodes by their largest weight puts the preferred articulator first almost by construction. The outcome follows the criterion; that single electrodes have a clear preferred articulator beyond what the grouping gives is not shown by it.

fig3d-timing-sequence¶

Articulator correlations follow a staggered sequence consistent across subjects; lip and tongue correlations begin well before sound onset, jaw and larynx align to the C-V transition, and the high and back tongue vowel features peak near the vowel midpoint (~250 ms).

Acoustic onset: the dandiset has no audio, so the onset of each CV is taken from the hand-marked syllable start of the trial table (mean over renditions, then over CVs). The criterion allows this substitute since the reader's answer, as a deviation from the prototype and thresholding of the Methods, with the result against t = 0 shown beside it.

for s in B.SUBJECTS:
    for b in blocks[s]:
        k = b["kept"]
        for lab, st, cv in zip(b["condition"][k], b["start"][k], b["cv"][k]):
            p = B.parse_label(lab)
            if p:
                onsets.append({"subject": s, "cv": p, "onset_ms": 1000 * (st - cv)})
onsets = pd.DataFrame(onsets)
per_cv = onsets.groupby(["subject", "cv"]).onset_ms.mean()
ACOUSTIC_ONSET = per_cv.mean()
print(f"Acoustic onset, substitute from the hand-marked syllable starts: mean over {len(per_cv)} CVs {ACOUSTIC_ONSET:.1f} ms "
      f"(per subject {per_cv.groupby(level=0).mean().round(1).to_dict()}; CV range {per_cv.min():.0f} to {per_cv.max():.0f} ms)")


def fig3d_table(TIM):
    """The criterion under every reading, from timing tables {(baseline, CVs, reading): rows}."""
    f3 = []
    for base in BASES:
        for cs in CVSETS:
            for reading in TIMING_READINGS:
                t = TIM[base, cs, reading]
                for anova in ("onset", "peak"):
                    F, p = stats.f_oneway(*[t[t.articulator == a][anova] for a in ART6])
                    mo = t.groupby("articulator").onset.mean()
                    mp = t.groupby("articulator").peak.mean()
                    c1 = mo["Lips"] < ACOUSTIC_ONSET and mo["Tongue"] < ACOUSTIC_ONSET
                    c2 = min(mo["Jaw"], mo["Larynx"]) > max(mo["Lips"], mo["Tongue"])
                    c3 = all(abs(mp[a] - 250) <= 25 for a in B.VOWEL_ARTICULATORS)
                    c1_0 = mo["Lips"] < 0 and mo["Tongue"] < 0
                    n_ok, n_ok0 = c1 + c2 + c3, c1_0 + c2 + c3
                    outcome = ("reproduced" if p < 1e-10 and n_ok == 3 else
                               "partially" if p < 1e-10 and n_ok == 2 else "not reproduced")
                    outcome0 = ("reproduced" if p < 1e-10 and n_ok0 == 3 else
                                "partially" if p < 1e-10 and n_ok0 == 2 else "not reproduced")
                    f3.append({"baseline": base, "CVs": cs, "timing reading": " / ".join(reading), "ANOVA on": anova,
                               "n": len(t), **{f"n {a[:6]}": int((t.articulator == a).sum()) for a in ART6},
                               "F": round(F, 1), "p": p, **{f"onset {a[:6]}": round(mo.get(a, np.nan)) for a in ART6},
                               "peak Back": round(mp["Back Tongue"]), "peak High": round(mp["High Tongue"]),
                               "lips,tongue < acoustic": c1, "jaw,larynx later": c2, "vowel peaks 250+-25": c3,
                               "outcome": outcome, "lips,tongue < 0": c1_0, "outcome vs t = 0": outcome0})
    return pd.DataFrame(f3)

Result: not reproduced. Under every one of the 96 readings none of the three order conditions holds, against the substitute acoustic onset (-110 ms) and against t = 0 alike. The lips correlations begin before the substitute onset (mean lips onset -270 to -54 ms), but the tongue correlations begin at -26 to +290 ms, so lips and tongue both precede the substitute onset in no reading and precede t = 0 in 2 of 96; the jaw begins as early as the lips (-270 to -116 ms), not later; and the high-tongue peak is at 276 to 325 ms, outside 250 +- 25 ms. The ANOVA across the six articulators has F = 9.4 to 39.2, with p below 1e-10 in 76 of the 96 readings. Electrode counts are 162 to 226 (paper 211). Tongue electrodes number 2 to 7 under the readings with one threshold for all six articulators (2 to 45 over all readings), so the tongue onsets of those readings rest on few electrodes. Leaving out the trials that overlap intervals marked as ECoG artifacts (a variant, not a reading) gives the same outcome: one condition holds in 4 of 96 readings and none in the others, with mean lips onsets of -338 to -125 ms and tongue onsets of -6 to 289 ms.

pca-nine-components¶

The cortical state-space has nine spatial PCs in every subject, the eigenvalues falling fast up to the ninth and slowly after, together explaining about 60% of the variance.

In [19]:

for base in BASES:

        for cs in CVSETS:
            for w in [(-500, 750), (-375, 620)]:
                fr = {s: STATE[s, base, z, cs, w][1] for s in B.SUBJECTS}
                pc.append({"baseline": base, "z-scoring": z, "CVs": cs, "window": f"{w[0]} to {w[1]}",
                           **{s: round(fr[s][:9].sum(), 3) for s in B.SUBJECTS},
                           "mean": round(np.mean([fr[s][:9].sum() for s in B.SUBJECTS]), 3)})
pc = pd.DataFrame(pc)
pc["within 0.54-0.66"] = pc["mean"].between(0.54, 0.66)

Result: blocked (methods_underspecified). With row z-scoring, the first nine PCs explain a mean of 0.60 to 0.66 over subjects, within 0.54 to 0.66 in 11 of 12 readings (rest, every CV and the -375 to 620 ms window gives 0.661). With time z-scoring, the mean is 0.49 to 0.56, within the tolerance under the rest baseline (4 readings) and once under whole, and below it in the other 7 readings. The readings give different outcomes (16 within, 8 not). The z-scoring decides most of the split (row 11 of 12 within, time 5 of 12); the CV set and the window do not change the count (8 of 12 within each). The variance explained does not depend on the input projected. The spectra show no sharp change at the ninth eigenvalue in any subject (printed values); that part is not judged.

fig4a-consonant-clusters¶

At the consonant time (-25 ms) k-means clustering of the cortical state-space groups syllables by major oral articulator, and three clusters are more parsimonious than two or four (mean silhouette 0.47 against 0.45 and 0.43).

In [20]:
tc, tv = B.ms_index(-25), B.ms_index(250)
sil = []
for base, z, pj, cs in SS_READINGS:
    for s in B.SUBJECTS:
        K = KS[s, base, z, pj, cs][:, :, tc]
        row = {"baseline": base, "z-scoring": z, "projection": pj, "CVs": cs, "subject": s}
        for k in (2, 3, 4):
            row[f"k={k}"] = silhouette_score(K, B.kmeans(K, k, seed=40 + k))
        sil.append(row)
sil = pd.DataFrame(sil)
print(sil.round(3).to_string(index=False))
means = sil.groupby(["baseline", "z-scoring", "projection", "CVs"])[["k=2", "k=3", "k=4"]].mean()
means["k=3 highest"] = means.idxmax(axis=1) == "k=3"
means["all within 10%"] = (abs(means["k=2"] - 0.45) <= 0.045) & (abs(means["k=3"] - 0.47) <= 0.047) & (abs(means["k=4"] - 0.43) <= 0.043)
print("\nMean over subjects (paper 0.45, 0.47, 0.43):")
print(means.round(3).to_string())
means["outcome"] = ["reproduced" if h and w else "partially" if h else "not reproduced"
                    for h, w in zip(means["k=3 highest"], means["all within 10%"])]
print("Outcome over readings:", overall(means.outcome))
by_factor(means.reset_index(), ["baseline", "z-scoring", "projection", "CVs"])
print("Reading with the highest mean silhouette, by k, over the 24 readings:", means[["k=2", "k=3", "k=4"]].idxmax(axis=1).value_counts().to_dict())

Result: blocked (methods_underspecified). In 23 of the 24 readings three clusters do not have the highest mean silhouette (not reproduced). In one, rest baseline, time z-scoring, projection (i) and every CV, k = 3 is highest by a small margin (0.333 against 0.329 for k = 2), with values outside tolerance (partially reproduced), so the readings differ. Over the 24 readings, k = 2 has the highest mean silhouette in 20, k = 4 in 3 and k = 3 in 1. The silhouettes are lower than the paper's under every reading (k = 3: 0.19 to 0.36 against 0.47). GP31's k = 2 silhouette is 0.35 to 0.80 with every CV, where its /thi/ has two renditions, and 0.24 to 0.68 with only CVs of 15 or more renditions.

suppfig11-co-clustering¶

Clusters of the cortical state-space match the major articulators at the consonant time (median co-clustering 0.50 against 0.32 by chance) and the vowels at the vowel time (0.65 against 0.37), across subjects.

In [21]:
rng = np.random.default_rng(11)
cc = []
for base, z, pj, cs in SS_READINGS:
    obs = {"cons a": [], "cons b": [], "vowel": []}
    null = {"cons a": [], "cons b": [], "vowel": []}
    for s in B.SUBJECTS:
        K = KS[s, base, z, pj, cs]
        nc_c = B.kmeans(K[:, :, tc], 3, seed=21)
        nc_v = B.kmeans(K[:, :, tv], 3, seed=22)
        for name, nc, labs in (("cons a", nc_c, [B.MAJOR["a"].get(c) for c, v in CVS[s, cs]]),
                               ("cons b", nc_c, [B.MAJOR["b"].get(c) for c, v in CVS[s, cs]]),
                               ("vowel", nc_v, [v for c, v in CVS[s, cs]])):
            keep = np.array([l is not None for l in labs])
            ac = np.array([l for l in labs if l is not None])
            ncs = nc[keep]
            obs[name].append(B.co_clustering(ncs, ac))
            null[name].append(np.mean([B.co_clustering(ncs, rng.permutation(ac)) for _ in range(1000)], axis=0))
    row = {"baseline": base, "z-scoring": z, "projection": pj, "CVs": cs}
    test_ok = {}
    for name in obs:
        o, n = np.concatenate(obs[name]), np.concatenate(null[name])
        p = stats.wilcoxon(o, n).pvalue
        row[f"{name}: n, obs, null, p"] = f"{len(o)}, {np.median(o):.3f}, {np.median(n):.3f}, {p:.1e}"
        test_ok[name] = bool(p < 1e-10 and np.median(o - n) > 0)
    for cons in ("cons a", "cons b"):
        ok_tests = test_ok[cons] and test_ok["vowel"]     # each label reading with its own consonant test
        mo = {k: np.median(np.concatenate(obs[k])) for k in (cons, "vowel")}
        mn = {k: np.median(np.concatenate(null[k])) for k in (cons, "vowel")}
        within = abs(mo[cons] - 0.50) <= 0.05 and abs(mn[cons] - 0.32) <= 0.032 and abs(mo["vowel"] - 0.65) <= 0.065 and abs(mn["vowel"] - 0.37) <= 0.037
        row[f"outcome ({cons[-1]})"] = "reproduced" if ok_tests and within else ("partially" if ok_tests else "not reproduced")
    cc.append(row)
cc = pd.DataFrame(cc)
print(cc.to_string(index=False))
print("Expected: consonants 0.50 +- 0.05 against 0.32 +- 0.032; vowels 0.65 +- 0.065 against 0.37 +- 0.037; p < 1e-10")
print("Outcome over readings:", overall(list(cc["outcome (a)"]) + list(cc["outcome (b)"])))
cc_long = pd.concat([cc.assign(labels=lr, outcome=cc[f"outcome ({lr})"]) for lr in ("a", "b")])
by_factor(cc_long, ["baseline", "z-scoring", "projection", "CVs", "labels"])
for name in ("cons a", "cons b", "vowel"):

Result: blocked (methods_underspecified). The state-space clusters match the major articulators more than chance under every reading (consonant p from 9e-23 to 3e-13). The observed consonant medians (0.633 to 0.909 with labels (a), 0.595 to 0.800 with labels (b)) are above the paper's 0.50 +- 0.05, and the vowel medians (0.41 to 0.70) are mostly below its 0.65 +- 0.065, so 38 of the 48 readings (24 readings by two label readings) give partially reproduced. In five readings, all with projection (i) (row with 15+ CVs under each baseline, rest with row and every CV, and rest with time and 15+ CVs), the vowel test misses the p < 1e-10 bound (p from 3e-10 to 5e-07) and gives not reproduced under both label readings. Projection (ii) gives partially reproduced in all 24 of its readings. Each label reading is now judged with its own consonant test and the vowel test; the outcomes are the same as before. The nulls (0.336 to 0.412 for consonants, 0.343 to 0.430 for vowels) are near the paper's 0.32 and 0.37.

fig4c-d-hierarchy¶

Hierarchical clustering of the state-space puts the major oral articulator at the top tier for consonants; for vowels the first split is lip rounding (/u/ against /a/ and /i/).

In [22]:
hc = []
for base, z, pj, cs in SS_READINGS:
    for s in B.SUBJECTS:
        K = KS[s, base, z, pj, cs]
        cons_cut = fcluster(linkage(K[:, :, tc], "ward"), 3, "maxclust")
        vow_cut = fcluster(linkage(K[:, :, tv], "ward"), 2, "maxclust")
        row = {"baseline": base, "z-scoring": z, "projection": pj, "CVs": cs, "subject": s}
        for lr in ("a", "b"):
            labs = np.array([B.MAJOR[lr].get(c, "") for c, v in CVS[s, cs]])
            lab = labs != ""
            maj = {k: pd.Series(labs[lab & (cons_cut == k)]).mode().tolist() for k in (1, 2, 3)}
            distinct = all(len(v) == 1 for v in maj.values()) and len({v[0] for v in maj.values()}) == 3
            home = {a: pd.Series(cons_cut[lab & (labs == a)]).mode()[0] for a in ("labial", "coronal", "dorsal")}
            purity = np.mean([cons_cut[i] == home[labs[i]] for i in np.where(lab)[0]])
            row[f"cons ({lr}) majorities"] = "/".join(v[0] if len(v) == 1 else "tie" for v in maj.values())
            row[f"cons ({lr}) in home"] = round(purity, 2)
            row[f"cons ({lr}) holds"] = bool(distinct and purity >= 2 / 3)
            row[f"cons ({lr}) co-clust"] = round(np.median(B.co_clustering(cons_cut[lab], labs[lab])), 2)
        vow = np.array([v for c, v in CVS[s, cs]])
        ok = any((vow_cut[vow == "u"] == ku).mean() > 0.5 and (vow_cut[vow != "u"] == 3 - ku).mean() > 0.5 for ku in (1, 2))
        row["a/i/u in cluster 1"] = "/".join(f"{(vow_cut[vow == v] == 1).mean():.2f}" for v in "aiu")
        row["vowel holds"] = bool(ok)
        hc.append(row)
hc = pd.DataFrame(hc)
print(hc.to_string(index=False))
oc = []
for (base, z, pj, cs), g in hc.groupby(["baseline", "z-scoring", "projection", "CVs"]):

                   "outcome": "reproduced" if both.all() else ("partially" if both.any() else "not reproduced")})
oc = pd.DataFrame(oc)
print(oc.to_string(index=False))

by_factor(oc, ["baseline", "z-scoring", "projection", "CVs", "labels"])

Result: blocked (methods_underspecified). Both splits hold together in at most one subject, EC2 (14 of the 24 readings), so no reading gives reproduced; 28 of the 48 readings (with the two label readings) give partially reproduced and 20 not reproduced. Under time z-scoring with projection (i) no subject meets both. The vowel split (/u/ against /a/ and /i/) never holds in GP31. By reading factor, projection (ii) gives partially reproduced in 20 of 24 readings and projection (i) in 8 of 24; the CV set and the label reading do not change the counts (14 of 24 each).

fig4ef-feature-correlations¶

Over early times (-375 to 120 ms) constriction location correlates with the state-space structure more than constriction degree, which correlates more than the upcoming vowel; over later times (125 to 620 ms) vowel configuration correlates most.

In [23]:
FEATS = ("location", "degree", "vowel")


def feature_r(base, z, pj, cs, metric="euclidean"):
    """R(t) per subject and feature set (Methods Eq. 7): {(subject, set): R over epoch times}."""
    out = {}
    for s in B.SUBJECTS:
        K = KS[s, base, z, pj, cs]
        dK = np.array([pdist(K[:, :, t]) for t in range(K.shape[2])])
        for f in FEATS:
            dP = pdist(B.feature_matrix(CVS[s, cs], f), metric)
            out[s, f] = np.array([np.corrcoef(d, dP)[0, 1] for d in dK])
    return out


early = (B.EPOCH_MS >= -375) & (B.EPOCH_MS < 120)
late = (B.EPOCH_MS >= 125) & (B.EPOCH_MS < 620)
RT = {k: feature_r(*k) for k in SS_READINGS}
fe = []
for (base, z, pj, cs), R in RT.items():
    for metric in ("euclidean", "hamming"):
        Rm = R if metric == "euclidean" else feature_r(base, z, pj, cs, "hamming")
        e = {f: np.concatenate([Rm[s, f][early] for s in B.SUBJECTS]) for f in FEATS}
        l = {f: np.concatenate([Rm[s, f][late] for s in B.SUBJECTS]) for f in FEATS}
        tests = {"early loc>deg": (e["location"], e["degree"]), "early deg>vow": (e["degree"], e["vowel"]),
                 "late vow>loc": (l["vowel"], l["location"]), "late vow>deg": (l["vowel"], l["degree"])}
        row = {"baseline": base, "z-scoring": z, "projection": pj, "CVs": cs, "distance": metric, "n": len(e["location"])}
        n_ok = 0
        for name, (a, b) in tests.items():
            p = stats.wilcoxon(a, b).pvalue
            ok = bool(np.median(a - b) > 0 and p < 1e-10)
            row[name] = f"{np.median(a - b):+.3f} p={p:.0e} {'Y' if ok else 'n'}"
            n_ok += ok
        row["med early L/D/V"] = "/".join(f"{np.median(e[f]):.2f}" for f in FEATS)
        row["med late L/D/V"] = "/".join(f"{np.median(l[f]):.2f}" for f in FEATS)
        row["outcome"] = "reproduced" if n_ok == 4 else ("partially" if n_ok else "not reproduced")
        fe.append(row)
fe = pd.DataFrame(fe)
print(fe.to_string(index=False))
print("Outcome over readings (Euclidean; Hamming is a variant):", overall(fe[fe.distance == "euclidean"].outcome))
by_factor(fe[fe.distance == "euclidean"], ["baseline", "z-scoring", "projection", "CVs"])

Result: blocked (methods_underspecified). In the early window, constriction location correlates with the state-space distances more than constriction degree, and degree more than the vowel, with p < 1e-10 under every reading with Euclidean distances except two (rest, projection (i), 15+ CVs, where location over degree has p = 3e-05 and 3e-04). In the late window the vowel features correlate more than both other sets with p < 1e-10 in 10 of the 24 readings (reproduced): every 15+ reading with projection (ii), pre and whole with time, projection (i) and 15+ CVs, and rest with projection (ii) and every CV. In the other 14 the late comparisons fail in part (partially reproduced), mostly with every CV, where location correlates as much as or more than the vowel features. By reading factor, projection (ii) gives 8 of the 10 reproduced readings and the 15+ CVs 8 of 10. Hamming distances, a variant, are in the table and are not judged.

fig5c-separability-timing¶

Cluster separability, averaged over subjects, rises from about -300 ms and peaks about 200 ms before the C-V transition for consonants, and rises from about 50 ms and peaks at +250 ms for vowels.

In [24]:
rng5 = np.random.default_rng(5)
N_BOOT = 1000


def cluster_labels(s, cs, K, which, kind):
    """Labels per CV (per time and CV for k-means); -1 for CVs without a label."""
    cvs = CVS[s, cs]
    if kind == "kmeans":
        return np.array([B.kmeans(K[:, :, t], 3, seed=1000 + t, n_init=10) for t in range(K.shape[2])])
    if which == "vowel":
        return np.array(["aiu".index(v) for c, v in cvs])
    lr = kind[-1]
    names = {"labial": 0, "coronal": 1, "dorsal": 2}
    out = []
    for c, v in cvs:
        m = B.MAJOR[lr].get(c)
        out.append(3 if kind.startswith("four") and c in B.SIBILANTS else (names[m] if m else -1))
    return np.array(out)


SEP_KINDS = {"consonant": ["groups a", "groups b", "four a", "four b", "kmeans"], "vowel": ["groups", "kmeans"]}


def separability_curves(base, z, pj, cs):
    out = {}
    kmeans_cache = {}
    for which, kinds in SEP_KINDS.items():
        for kind in kinds:
            curves, boots = [], []
            for s in B.SUBJECTS:
                K = KS[s, base, z, pj, cs]
                if kind == "kmeans":
                    if s not in kmeans_cache:
                        kmeans_cache[s] = cluster_labels(s, cs, K, which, kind)
                    lab = kmeans_cache[s]
                else:
                    lab = cluster_labels(s, cs, K, which, kind)
                keep = (lab >= 0) if lab.ndim == 1 else np.ones(K.shape[0], bool)
                Ks = K[keep]
                labk = lab[keep] if lab.ndim == 1 else lab[:, keep]
                D = np.array([squareform(pdist(Ks[:, :, t])) for t in range(Ks.shape[2])])
                curves.append(B.separability(D, labk)[0])
                wts = rng5.multinomial(len(Ks), np.ones(len(Ks)) / len(Ks), size=N_BOOT)
                boots.append(B.separability(D, labk, wts))
            out[which, kind] = (np.mean(curves, 0), np.mean(boots, 0).std(0), curves)
    return out


SEP = {k: separability_curves(*k) for k in SS_READINGS}


def onset_peak(curve, se):
    """Peak time, onset (a) first time above the level at -500 ms by 2 bootstrap s.e., onset (b)
    first time of the run up to the peak above half the peak value."""
    p = int(np.argmax(curve))
    above = np.where(curve[:p + 1] > curve[0] + 2 * se[:p + 1])[0]
    on_a = B.EPOCH_MS[above[0]] if len(above) else np.nan
    below = np.where(curve[:p + 1] < curve[p] / 2)[0]
    on_b = B.EPOCH_MS[below[-1] + 1] if len(below) else np.nan
    return B.EPOCH_MS[p], on_a, on_b


sp = []
for (base, z, pj, cs), d in SEP.items():
    for ck in SEP_KINDS["consonant"]:
        vk = "kmeans" if ck == "kmeans" else "groups"
        cpk, con_a, con_b = onset_peak(d["consonant", ck][0], d["consonant", ck][1])
        vpk, von_a, von_b = onset_peak(d["vowel", vk][0], d["vowel", vk][1])
        peaks_ok = abs(cpk + 200) <= 20 and abs(vpk - 250) <= 25
        ons_ok = {"a": abs(con_a + 300) <= 30 and abs(von_a - 50) <= 10, "b": abs(con_b + 300) <= 30 and abs(von_b - 50) <= 10}
        sp.append({"baseline": base, "z-scoring": z, "projection": pj, "CVs": cs, "clusters": f"{ck} | {vk}",
                   "cons peak": cpk, "cons onset a": con_a, "cons onset b": con_b,
                   "vowel peak": vpk, "vowel onset a": von_a, "vowel onset b": von_b,
                   "peaks ok": peaks_ok, "onset ok a": ons_ok["a"], "onset ok b": ons_ok["b"],
                   "outcome": "reproduced" if peaks_ok and any(ons_ok.values()) else ("partially" if peaks_ok else "not reproduced")})
sp = pd.DataFrame(sp)
print(sp.to_string(index=False))
print("Expected: consonant peak -200 +- 20, onset -300 +- 30; vowel peak 250 +- 25, onset 50 +- 10 ms")
print("Outcome over readings:", overall(sp.outcome))
by_factor(sp, ["baseline", "z-scoring", "projection", "CVs", "clusters"])
g = sp[~sp.clusters.str.startswith("kmeans")]
print("Phonetic-group readings: consonant peak", g["cons peak"].min(), "to", g["cons peak"].max(), "| vowel peak", g["vowel peak"].min(), "to", g["vowel peak"].max(),
      "| consonant onset (a)", g["cons onset a"].min(), "to", g["cons onset a"].max(), "| (b)", g["cons onset b"].min(), "to", g["cons onset b"].max(),

Result: not reproduced. Under none of the 120 readings (24 baseline, z-scoring, projection and CV readings by five cluster readings) are both peaks within tolerance. With the phonetic groups the consonant separability peaks at -155 to +15 ms (paper -200 +- 20) and the vowel separability at 155 to 235 ms (paper 250 +- 25, within it in some readings); with k-means at each time one curve serves both, peaking anywhere from -170 to 375 ms. The consonant onsets (reading a, -375 to -180 ms) reach the paper's -300 +- 30 ms under some readings, and the vowel onsets (55 to 105 ms) are mostly later than its 50 +- 10 ms. The bootstrap no longer pairs a token with its own copies, which changes only the s.e. used by onset reading (a); no reading gives both peaks within tolerance under any reading factor (table of counts).

fig5d-separability-coupling¶

Cluster separability and the correlation of the state-space with phonetic features are tightly linked over time for consonants and vowels in each subject (R2 0.42 to 0.98, all P < 1e-10).

In [25]:
c5 = []
for (base, z, pj, cs), d in SEP.items():
    R = RT[base, z, pj, cs]
    for ck in SEP_KINDS["consonant"]:
        vk = "kmeans" if ck == "kmeans" else "groups"
        for rmode in ("(a) matching set", "(b) mean of three"):
            vals = []
            for i, s in enumerate(B.SUBJECTS):
                for which, kind, fset in (("consonant", ck, "location"), ("vowel", vk, "vowel")):
                    r = R[s, fset] if rmode.startswith("(a)") else np.mean([R[s, f] for f in FEATS], 0)
                    res = stats.pearsonr(d[which, kind][2][i], r)
                    vals.append((res.statistic ** 2, res.pvalue, res.statistic))
            r2 = np.array([v[0] for v in vals]); ps = np.array([v[1] for v in vals]); rs = np.array([v[2] for v in vals])
            ok = bool((r2 >= 0.378).all() and (ps < 1e-10).all() and (rs > 0).all())
            part = bool((rs > 0).all() and (ps < 1e-10).all())
            c5.append({"baseline": base, "z-scoring": z, "projection": pj, "CVs": cs, "clusters": f"{ck} | {vk}", "R": rmode,
                       "R2 (EC2 c,v GP31 c,v GP33 c,v)": " ".join(f"{x:.2f}" for x in r2),
                       "max p": ps.max(), "min r": round(rs.min(), 2),
                       "outcome": "reproduced" if ok else ("partially" if part else "not reproduced")})
c5 = pd.DataFrame(c5)
print(c5.to_string(index=False))
print("\nOutcome over readings:", overall(c5.outcome))
by_factor(c5, ["baseline", "z-scoring", "projection", "CVs", "clusters", "R"])
print("Outcomes by reading of the clusters and of R:")
print(c5.groupby(["clusters", "R"]).outcome.value_counts().unstack(fill_value=0).to_string())

Result: blocked (methods_underspecified). With the phonetic groups as clusters and the matching feature set for R (constriction location for consonants, vowel features for vowels), the six R2 values lie within 0.38 to 1 with p < 1e-10 in 80 of 96 readings, are positive and significant with some below 0.38 in 15, and fail in 1 (R2 0.14 to 0.99 over these readings). With the mean of the three feature sets, or with k-means clusters at each time, the coupling fails in every reading. The readings of the claim give different outcomes, and two of them decide the split: the reading of R (with the mean of three feature sets all 120 readings fail) and the reading of the clusters (with k-means clusters all 48 readings fail, the 24 with the matching feature set among them). Every level of the baseline, z-scoring, projection and CV set has both reproduced and not reproduced readings.

suppfig13-consonant-vowel-distance¶

Consonant and vowel representations occupy distinct regions of the state-space; consonant-vowel distances are larger than consonant-consonant and vowel-vowel distances, and consonant-consonant distances are larger than vowel-vowel ones.

cvd = []
for base, z, pj, cs in SS_READINGS:
    for reading in ("(a) mean of cross pairings", "(b) i at -25, j at +250"):
        CC, VV, CVd = [], [], []
        for s in B.SUBJECTS:
            K = KS[s, base, z, pj, cs]
            Kc, Kv = K[:, :, tc], K[:, :, tv]
            i, j = np.triu_indices(len(Kc), 1)
            CC.append(np.linalg.norm(Kc[i] - Kc[j], axis=1))
            VV.append(np.linalg.norm(Kv[i] - Kv[j], axis=1))
            d1 = np.linalg.norm(Kc[i] - Kv[j], axis=1)
            d2 = np.linalg.norm(Kc[j] - Kv[i], axis=1)
            CVd.append((d1 + d2) / 2 if reading.startswith("(a)") else d1)
        CC, VV, CVd = map(np.concatenate, (CC, VV, CVd))
        row = {"baseline": base, "z-scoring": z, "projection": pj, "CVs": cs, "CV distance": reading, "pairs": len(CC),
               "median CC": round(np.median(CC), 2), "median VV": round(np.median(VV), 2), "median CV": round(np.median(CVd), 2)}
        ok = True
        for name, (a, b) in {"CV>CC": (CVd, CC), "CV>VV": (CVd, VV), "CC>VV": (CC, VV)}.items():
            p = min(1.0, 3 * stats.wilcoxon(a, b).pvalue)
            row[name] = f"{np.median(a - b):+.2f} p={p:.0e}"
            ok &= bool(np.median(a - b) > 0 and p < 1e-10)
        row["orderings hold"] = ok
        # The criterion defines only reproduced. A reading where the orderings hold and only the pair
        # count differs is counted as partially reproduced (the effect holds, the data differ), by the
        # protocol's general definition; one where an ordering fails, as not reproduced.
        row["outcome"] = ("reproduced" if ok and len(CC) == 4623 else "partially" if ok else "not reproduced")
        cvd.append(row)

Result: blocked (methods_underspecified). Under row z-scoring, and under time z-scoring with projection (ii), consonant-vowel distances exceed consonant-consonant ones, which exceed vowel-vowel ones, with corrected p < 1e-10. Under time z-scoring with projection (i) the consonant-vowel distances are shorter than the consonant-consonant ones, in every baseline and CV set (12 of 12 readings). The number of pairs is 4677 with every CV and 4567 with CVs of 15 or more renditions, never the paper's 4623, so no reading meets the criterion as written (0 of 48). The criterion defines only reproduced; this attempt counts a reading where all orderings hold and only the pair count differs as partially reproduced (36 of 48), by the protocol's general definition of an effect that holds in part, and one where an ordering fails as not reproduced (12). The pair count is fixed by the dataset's syllables (data-composition), while the orderings depend on the z-scoring and projection readings, which the paper does not fix; the outcome is blocked for that.

suppfig9-pc-articulator-weights¶

The first three PCs are weighted toward tongue over lips, and toward lips over jaw and larynx, while jaw and larynx do not differ.

Note on the method: by Methods Eq. 6, log10|PCw_ij| = log10|M_ij| + log10|W_jA|, so for a given electrode the PC term is the same for every articulator and cancels in the paired comparisons; the tests give the same result in every PC.

pairs6 = list(itertools.combinations(range(4), 2))
s9 = []
for (base, cs, reading, pmode) in W_READINGS:
    for z in ZMODES:
        for eset in ("all vSMC", "GLM electrodes"):
            if eset == "all vSMC" and pmode == "t-test":
                continue    # the p-value reading only changes which electrodes are kept
            vals = []
            for s in B.SUBJECTS:
                w = WEIGHTS[base, cs, reading, pmode][s]
                M = STATE[s, base, z, cs, EP][0]
                sel = w["keep"] if eset == "GLM electrodes" else np.ones(len(w["keep"]), bool)
                vals.append(np.log10(np.abs(M[sel, :3, None] * w["W"][sel, None, :])))
            V = np.concatenate(vals)            # (electrode, PC, articulator)
            n_in = len(V)
            V = V[np.isfinite(V).all(axis=(1, 2))]   # electrodes without a window T_A for an articulator are dropped
            per_pc, meds = [], []
            for pci in range(3):
                p = {(a, b): (np.median(V[:, pci, a] - V[:, pci, b]), min(1.0, 6 * stats.wilcoxon(V[:, pci, a], V[:, pci, b]).pvalue))
                     for a, b in pairs6}

                def greater(a, b, alpha):
                    m, pv = p[(a, b)] if (a, b) in p else (-p[(b, a)][0], p[(b, a)][1])
                    return bool(m > 0 and pv < alpha)
                L, T, X, J = 0, 1, 2, 3
                ra = greater(L, J, 0.001) and greater(L, X, 0.001)
                rb = ra and greater(T, J, 0.001) and greater(T, X, 0.001)
                per_pc.append(greater(T, L, 0.05) and (ra or rb) and p[(X, J)][1] > 0.05)
                meds.append("/".join(f"{np.median(V[:, pci, a]):.2f}" for a in range(4)))
            n_ok = sum(per_pc)
            s9.append({"baseline": base, "CVs": cs, "timing reading": " / ".join(reading), "p-value": pmode, "z-scoring": z,
                       "electrodes": eset, "n": len(V), "dropped": n_in - len(V), "PC1 medians L/T/X/J": meds[0], "PCs holding": "".join("Y" if x else "n" for x in per_pc),
                       "outcome": "reproduced" if n_ok == 3 else ("partially" if n_ok else "not reproduced")})
s9 = pd.DataFrame(s9)
print(s9.to_string(index=False))
print("\nOutcome over readings:", overall(s9.outcome))
print("Electrodes dropped for lack of a window T_A: 0 in", int((s9.dropped == 0).sum()), "readings, up to", int(s9.dropped.max()),
      "| n from", int(s9.n.min()), "to", int(s9.n.max()))
base, cs, reading, pmode, z = "pre", "all", TIMING_READINGS[2], "F-test", "row"
V = np.concatenate([np.log10(np.abs(STATE[s, base, z, cs, EP][0][:, :3, None] * WEIGHTS[base, cs, reading, pmode][s]["W"][:, None, :])) for s in B.SUBJECTS])
V = V[np.isfinite(V).all(axis=(1, 2))]
for pci in range(3):
    ps = {f"{B.ARTICULATORS[a][:2]}-{B.ARTICULATORS[b][:2]}": f"{np.median(V[:, pci, a] - V[:, pci, b]):+.2f} p={min(1, 6 * stats.wilcoxon(V[:, pci, a], V[:, pci, b]).pvalue):.0e}" for a, b in pairs6}
    print(f"PC{pci + 1} ({base}, {cs}, {reading}, all vSMC, n={len(V)}): median paired differences and corrected p {ps}")

Result: not reproduced. Under all 288 readings the condition fails in all three PCs. In the reading printed in full (all 268 vSMC electrodes, pre, every CV), the tongue weights are not larger than the lips weights (median paired difference of log10 weights, lips minus tongue, +0.03, corrected p = 1), and jaw and larynx differ (corrected p = 5e-11). The input projected does not enter this test, which uses the PCs only. Electrodes without a window T_A for an articulator are dropped: none in 168 readings, up to 83 in the others (GP31 lacks a tongue window in some timing readings), leaving 32 to 268 electrodes.

A failure to reproduce here may be a failure of this attempt, not of the paper: see the reasoning and the differences from the paper's method.

How the analysis differs from the paper's. High gamma is computed here from the raw ECoG, as the Methods describe, with a filter bank whose widths the paper does not give (a standard choice) and with the dataset's bad-channel flags in place of the paper's inspection. The baseline for the z-scores is not given by the paper; the three readings of the claims file are run, the rest period the dataset marks among them. vSMC electrodes are those labelled precentral or postcentral (268, against the paper's 266). The acoustic onset of fig3d is the hand-marked syllable start, a substitute the criterion allows as a deviation since the audio is not in the dandiset; the result against t = 0 has the same outcome. The questions asked by this attempt were answered from the paper, which fixes none of the details asked about: whether CVs with fewer than 15 renditions are kept, how the state-space input is z-scored, and which input is projected onto the PCs are all left open, and every reading is run. The blocked outcomes of active-electrodes and of the state-space claims other than fig5d come from these readings giving different results; the paper cannot settle them. That of fig5d comes from the claims file's readings of R and of the clusters, which split it at every level of the readings above. The GLM weights used by fig1f-h, suppfig6 and suppfig9 come from claim fig2a-lips-dorsal, which is blocked for its spatial judgement only; the weights need no positions, so these claims are tested. Two variants that are not readings of the claims file are shown beside the results: leaving out trials that overlap intervals marked as ECoG artifacts (active-electrodes, fig3d), and the suppfig6 test on permuted weights.

What was found about the dataset. It holds four subjects; EC2, GP31 and GP33 fit the paper's EC2, EC31 and EC33 (assumed, not shown), and EC9 is not in the paper. The audio was removed. No electrode has a position relative to the central sulcus or the Sylvian fissure, and one of the three subjects (GP33) has no coordinates at all, so seven spatial findings cannot be tested. The coordinates of EC2 and GP31 have no unit or frame. GP31 has two renditions of /thi/ and none of /tha/ or /thu/, and up to 107 renditions of other CVs; EC2 has 10 of /thi/; the paper states 15 to 100 per CV. Two labels are misspelt (she, ha). Electrode ids start at 0 in EC2 and GP31 and at 1 in GP33 and EC9. 162 of the 9370 kept trials overlap intervals marked as ECoG artifacts, and leaving them out moves the active-electrode count of the one reading within tolerance out of it. The subject fields hold only species and id, and nothing links GP31 and GP33 to the paper's EC31 and EC33; GP33's electrode group is auto_group. One file (EC2 block 1) holds a power spectrum in a processing module.
